title: The future of music and satisfying the public
summary: He plays what the public likes and also for musicians.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What do you think, I mean from your vantage point and from all of the accomplishments that you've had in the field, and you're still working in it from here, and you have a very, you know, (inaudible) overview of all of the things. How do you see all of these different tastes and things sort of coming together? I mean, what would you think should
be the future of the music business in terms of meeting everybody's needs.

Well, that's a hard thing to figure out, the future, you know, of the music business. I'd just say I'll just keep playing like I'm playing, and try to get together with them the best I possibly could.

I play this tune, and if I'd be playing a dance number, and I have a certain amount of people there, on a ballad, if I play a swinging tune the next time, I'd have a few more. I just try to get to the needs of the majority. But, I just try to play something that I think will hit with them.
I don't know how to explain that to you right away on the needs of the music business. But, I just keep trying to think of some type of tunes that I think they may like.
Or, even try to pen some when I get back to that that I think the public may like. It don't care what tempo it is. But, you take a chance on that especially
when you're looking to satisfy the public. You take a chance, and sometimes you'll be lucky. But, I've been pretty fortunate through the years, you know, of getting some things that they liked.
Well, do you find that to be a very important thing from your standpoint? That of "satisfying the public"?

I do. I've always felt that way through the years, try to do something that you'd think they'd like. Instead of playing for myself, I try to play for them. You know? And then at the same time, I still can play for myself and play for the musicians too. You know, at the time when I see the talent to do that cause I like that. I want to be recognized by the musicians too, you know. But, when you're playing for the public, I kind of play what I think they'd like.
